Reusing the Existing Listeners

ticket.sla_breached gets its own domainEvents.on(...) block in each Week 5 listener file — no new notification machinery needed.

escalateOverdueTickets emits EVENTS.TICKET_SLA_BREACHED exactly the way createTicket/updateTicket emit their events — so the three listener files from Week 5 each just gain one more domainEvents.on(...) block, same as every event before it.

// Figure 6.8: in-app notification (src/events/listeners/notifyInApp.listener.js)
domainEvents.on(EVENTS.TICKET_SLA_BREACHED, async (ticket) => {
  try {
    if (ticket.assignedAgentId) {
      await prisma.notification.create({
        data: {
          userId: ticket.assignedAgentId,
          type: EVENTS.TICKET_SLA_BREACHED,
          message: `Ticket "${ticket.subject}" has breached its SLA and needs attention.`,
        },
      });
      return;
    }

    const admins = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { role: 'admin' }, select: { id: true } });
    await prisma.notification.createMany({
      data: admins.map((admin) => ({ userId: admin.id, type: EVENTS.TICKET_SLA_BREACHED, message: '...' })),
    });
  } catch (err) { /* ... */ }
});

Who gets notified depends on whether the ticket has an owner: an assigned ticket escalates to that one agent directly; an unassigned ticket has no one narrower to point at, so every admin gets it instead — a real escalation path, not just "the queue" the way ticket.created's agent fan-out works.

// Figure 6.9: email (src/events/listeners/notifyEmail.listener.js)
domainEvents.on(EVENTS.TICKET_SLA_BREACHED, async (ticket) => {
  try {
    if (!ticket.assignedAgentId) return;

    await mailer.sendMail({
      to: ticket.assignedAgent.email,
      subject: `SLA breached: ticket #${ticket.id} needs attention`,
      text: `Ticket "${ticket.subject}" has been open past its SLA threshold.`,
    });
  } catch (err) { /* ... */ }
});

Email deliberately doesn't mirror the admin fan-out: there's no email branch for the unassigned case, only a quiet return. An inbox that gets a message every time any ticket goes unassigned-and-overdue is exactly the kind of alert an admin learns to filter out or ignore — the in-app notification above (visible next time they open the dashboard) and the realtime push covered next already surface it there without the fatigue an email blast to every admin would cause.
